title: Telegram account
description: Acts as a connected Telegram user account over MTProto. Watches channels and groups, stores new posts, filters them by keywords and fires a telegram.feed trigger; and exposes a tool-pack so an agent can read dialogs, history, chats and participants, send text, media and albums, forward and copy messages, edit, delete, pin, react, join and leave chats and download attachments as the same account. The session comes from the bound telegram-user account; independent of the bot add-on: an organization can run only the feed, only the tools, or both.

permissions.reason: Keep the resident poller that reads new channel posts
Stay running to keep polling the watched channels
Fire telegram.feed instances for matching posts
Resolve the bound telegram-user account for the feed session and for every tool call
Read the MTProto session and the linked telegram-app credentials
Download media by https url when send_media, send_album or copy_message is given a url source instead of a workspace path; bytes are uploaded to Telegram and never stored by the add-on
Read attachments from the organization workspace to upload them with send_media and send_album
Save attachments downloaded by download_media into the organization workspace

fields.label: Channels and groups
fields.help: One @username, t.me link or numeric id per line

fields.label: Backfill posts on first sync
fields.help: How many of the newest posts to fire when a channel is first watched (0 keeps the history silent and only fires new posts)

fields.label: Allowed chats for tools
fields.help: Chat ids or @usernames the tools may touch, separated by commas or new lines. Empty means every chat the account can reach. A chat is matched by its id or its @username, so listing @name allows the same chat by its numeric id and the other way round. Tool calls to any other chat fail with permission_denied. Two exceptions: list_dialogs lists every dialog unfiltered, and join_chat by invite link is not checked (see join_allowed). The global search_messages (no chat) is limited by this list too: hits from chats that are not allowed are dropped and counted in the filteredOut field of the result. The feed poller is not affected.

fields.label: Read-only tools
fields.help: Reject every tool that writes: send_message, send_media, send_album, forward_message, copy_message, edit_message, delete_messages, pin_message, unpin_message, react, mark_read, join_chat, leave_chat, create_topic and download_media. The read tools (get_account, list_dialogs, list_messages, get_message, search_messages, get_chat, list_participants, list_topics) keep working, so an agent can watch chats without touching the account. Recommended for monitoring-only setups: a user account that only reads is far less likely to be restricted.

fields.label: Allow joining and leaving chats
fields.help: When off, join_chat and leave_chat fail with permission_denied. Joining by invite link is not checked against allowed_chats, so an open account can enter any chat its invite points at; turn this off for a locked-down account.

fields.label: Minimum interval between sends, ms
fields.help: Minimum gap between two messages sent to the same chat. Guards against one agent replying faster than a human would.

fields.label: Max sends per hour
fields.help: Account-wide cap over a rolling hour. Telegram restricts accounts that message too fast, so keep this low.

fields.label: Max sends per day
fields.help: Account-wide cap over a rolling 24 hours. One media upload, album or copy counts as one send, not per item.

fields.label: Max messages per history or search call
fields.help: Upper bound for the limit argument of list_messages and search_messages; larger values are rejected.

fields.label: Max dialogs per list_dialogs call
fields.help: Upper bound for the limit argument of list_dialogs; larger values are rejected.

fields.label: Max outgoing media size, MB
fields.help: Cap per media item uploaded by send_media, send_album and the caption re-upload of copy_message. Values above 50 fall back to 50. Media fetched by url is additionally capped at 8 MB by the host http.fetch limit.

fields.label: Max incoming media size, MB
fields.help: Cap for download_media and for the copy_message re-upload path. Values above 50 fall back to 50.

fields.label: Flood-wait retries inside a tool call
fields.help: 0 fails immediately with rate_limited and retry_after. 1-3 waits out a Telegram FLOOD_WAIT inside the call when the wait is 30 seconds or shorter, then retries once; longer waits still fail. Applies to text, media, album, copy, edit, delete and join calls alike.

descriptor.name: telegram-account
descriptor.title: Telegram account
descriptor.description: Read dialogs, history, chats and participants, send text, media and albums, forward, copy, edit, delete, pin and react, join and leave chats and download attachments as the connected Telegram user account (MTProto, not the bot API)

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Read the connected Telegram user account: numeric id, @username, first and last name, and phone when the session exposes it. Call it first to confirm which account the agent acts as before writing anything.

tools.name: list_dialogs
tools.description: List the account's dialogs (private chats, groups, supergroups, channels) in the order Telegram shows them. Each entry carries kind (user, group, supergroup, channel), peerId, username, title and unread count. limit defaults to 50 and cannot exceed max_dialogs from the add-on config. This tool is not filtered by allowed_chats.

limit.description: How many dialogs to return, default 50, capped by max_dialogs (200 by default)

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: Read the recent history of a chat, newest first. chat accepts @username, a t.me/... link or a numeric peer id and must pass allowed_chats. limit defaults to 20 and cannot exceed max_history_limit from the add-on config; beforeId returns messages older than that message id. Each message carries its id, ISO date, sender (@username, title or numeric id), text truncated to 2000 characters with truncated: true, and mediaKind when the message has media.

chat.description: @username, t.me/username, t.me/username/123 link or numeric peer id

limit.description: How many messages to return, default 20, capped by max_history_limit (100 by default)

beforeId.description: Return messages older than this message id, for paging back through history

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: Read one message by id: ISO date, sender, text truncated to 2000 characters, mediaKind, mediaSize in bytes, replyToMessageId, forwardFrom, views for channel posts and editedAt when it was edited. chat accepts @username, a t.me/... link or a numeric peer id and must pass allowed_chats.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageId.description: Id of the message, from list_messages or search_messages

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Search message text. With chat set the search runs inside that chat and the chat must pass allowed_chats; without chat it runs globally across every chat the account can see and each result carries peerId so the chat can be resolved, but hits from chats that do not pass allowed_chats are dropped and counted in filteredOut, so a global search never leaks a chat outside the grant. limit defaults to 20 and cannot exceed max_history_limit. Results carry the same fields as list_messages with the addition of mediaSize, replyToMessageId, forwardFrom, views and editedAt.

chat.description: Leave out for a global search; @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id to search one chat

limit.description: How many results to return, default 20, capped by max_history_limit (100 by default)

tools.name: get_chat
tools.description: Read one chat: title, kind, @username, about text, participantsCount, isMember, pinnedMessageId and slowmodeSeconds for supergroups. Fields Telegram does not expose for that chat type come back as null. chat accepts @username, a t.me/... link or a numeric peer id and must pass allowed_chats.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

tools.name: list_participants
tools.description: List participants of a group, supergroup or channel: numeric id, @username, display name, isBot and isAdmin. limit defaults to 50 and is capped at 200; search filters by name or username, adminsOnly keeps admins and creators. On basic groups the admin filter is applied locally because Telegram only filters participants server-side for channels. chat must pass allowed_chats.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

limit.description: How many participants to return, default 50, capped at 200

search.description: Only participants whose name or @username contains this text

adminsOnly.description: Keep only admins and creators, default false

tools.name: list_topics
tools.description: List forum topics of a supergroup with forums enabled: topic id (equal to its top message id), title, closed, pinned and unread count. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. A chat without forums fails with the Telegram error mapped to invalid_params. chat must pass allowed_chats.

chat.description: Forum supergroup: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

limit.description: How many topics to return, default 20, capped at 100

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a text message as the connected user account, up to 4096 characters. replyTo replies to a message id in the same chat, parseMode is none (default, text sent verbatim), markdown or html, silent suppresses the notification sound, scheduleAt is an ISO 8601 timestamp in the future and hands the message to Telegram's scheduler instead of sending it now. Respects allowed_chats, read_only, the send-rate limits and FLOOD_WAIT handling; returns the new messageId. Raising those limits risks a Telegram restriction on the account.

chat.description: @username, t.me/username, t.me/username/123 link or numeric peer id

replyTo.description: Message id in the same chat to reply to

parseMode.description: How Telegram parses the text, default none

silent.description: Send without a notification sound, default false

scheduleAt.description: ISO 8601 time in the future; Telegram sends the message then instead of now

tools.name: send_media
tools.description: Send one photo, video, document, audio track, voice note or gif with an optional caption of up to 1024 characters. source is either an https url (downloaded by the add-on) or a path inside the organization workspace; file://, http://, absolute paths and .. escapes are rejected. kind defaults to auto, which picks the kind from the file extension and mime type, and can be forced to photo, video, document, audio, voice or gif. The size is checked against max_upload_mb (20 MB by default) before upload; media taken from a url is additionally limited to 8 MB by the host. forceDocument hides the media preview, replyTo, silent and parseMode behave as in send_message. One call counts as one send towards the rate limits.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

source.description: https url or workspace-relative file path

kind.description: Media kind, default auto from the extension and mime type

replyTo.description: Message id in the same chat to reply to

silent.description: Send without a notification sound, default false

forceDocument.description: Send as a document even for photo and video files, default false

parseMode.description: How Telegram parses the caption, default none

tools.name: send_album
tools.description: Send 2 to 10 media items as one album in a single Telegram call. Each item carries source (https url or workspace path) and optional kind (auto by default) and caption of up to 1024 characters; the caption of the first item is the album caption. Per-item media attributes are preserved, so a gif stays an animation and a voice note stays a voice message. Every item is size-checked against max_upload_mb, and the whole album counts as one send towards the rate limits. replyTo, silent and parseMode apply to the album as a whole.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

source.description: https url or workspace-relative file path

replyTo.description: Message id in the same chat to reply to

silent.description: Send without a notification sound, default false

parseMode.description: How Telegram parses the captions, default none

tools.name: forward_message
tools.description: Forward one or more messages from one chat to another as the connected user account. messageIds holds up to 100 ids and messageId is the single-id form kept for compatibility; both chats must pass allowed_chats. dropAuthor removes the link back to the original author, silent suppresses the notification. One call counts as one send towards the rate limits; returns the new message ids in toChat.

fromChat.description: Source chat: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageId.description: Single message id to forward, kept for compatibility with earlier callers

messageIds.description: Up to 100 message ids to forward

toChat.description: Destination chat: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

dropAuthor.description: Forward without the original author, default false

silent.description: Forward without a notification sound, default false

tools.name: copy_message
tools.description: Copy one message to another chat. Without caption it forwards the message with the author dropped, which is one Telegram call and keeps media, formatting and links intact. With caption the forwarded text cannot be replaced, so the add-on downloads the media of the source message (bounded by the smaller of max_download_mb and max_upload_mb) and uploads it again with the new caption; a text-only message cannot be copied with a new caption and fails with invalid_params, so use send_message for that. Both chats must pass allowed_chats and the call counts as one send.

from.description: Source chat: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

to.description: Destination chat: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

caption.description: New caption; forces a download and re-upload of the media instead of a forward

parseMode.description: How Telegram parses the new caption, default none

silent.description: Send without a notification sound, default false

tools.name: edit_message
tools.description: Replace the text of a message the account sent, up to 4096 characters, with parseMode none (default), markdown or html. Telegram only allows editing your own messages and rejects edits that change nothing. Respects allowed_chats, read_only and the send-rate limits; counts as one send.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageId.description: Id of the message to edit

parseMode.description: How Telegram parses the new text, default none

tools.name: delete_messages
tools.description: Delete up to 100 messages of a chat by id. revoke defaults to true, which deletes the messages for everyone when the account is allowed to; set it to false to remove them only from this account's side. Telegram silently ignores ids it cannot delete, so the result lists exactly what was asked for. Respects allowed_chats, read_only and the send-rate limits; counts as one send.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageIds.description: Up to 100 message ids to delete

revoke.description: Delete for everyone, default true; false deletes only on this account's side

tools.name: pin_message
tools.description: Pin one message in a chat. notify defaults to false so the pin does not produce a notification for the members. The account needs pin rights, otherwise Telegram answers with CHAT_ADMIN_REQUIRED, which is reported as permission_denied. Respects allowed_chats and read_only.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageId.description: Id of the message to pin

notify.description: Notify members about the pin, default false

tools.name: unpin_message
tools.description: Unpin one message, or every pinned message in the chat when messageId is left out. Respects allowed_chats and read_only.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageId.description: Message id to unpin; leave out to unpin everything in the chat

tools.name: react
tools.description: Set a reaction on one message, or clear the reaction when emoji is an empty string. A single message can hold one reaction per account. The emoji is not validated against Telegram's allowed set here: an unsupported emoji comes back as the Telegram error mapped to invalid_params, and a chat that forbids reactions answers with a permission error. Respects allowed_chats and read_only.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageId.description: Id of the message to react to

emoji.description: One emoji, or an empty string to clear the reaction

tools.name: join_chat
tools.description: Join a chat with the connected account. link accepts an invite link (t.me/+hash, t.me/joinchat/hash) or an @username / t.me/username of a public channel or supergroup. Invite links are not checked against allowed_chats: joining is allowed whenever read_only is off and join_allowed is on, which is deliberate so an account can be pointed at a fresh private chat, but it does widen what the account can reach. Counts as one send towards the rate limits; returns the chat title when Telegram reveals it.

link.description: t.me/+hash or t.me/joinchat/hash invite link, or @username of a public chat

tools.name: leave_chat
tools.description: Leave a group, supergroup or channel. chat must pass allowed_chats. Basic groups are left with messages.deleteChatUser, channels and supergroups with channels.leaveChannel. Blocked together with join_chat by join_allowed. Respects read_only.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

tools.name: create_topic
tools.description: Create a forum topic in a supergroup with forums enabled and return its topic id, which doubles as the id of the topic's first message. title is up to 128 characters. The account needs the create-topics right. A chat without forums fails with CHANNEL_FORUM_MISSING mapped to invalid_params. chat must pass allowed_chats; this tool does not consume the send-rate budget.

chat.description: Forum supergroup: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

tools.name: download_media
tools.description: Download the media of one message into the organization workspace and return its path, size and mime type. path is relative to the workspace; absolute paths, .. escapes, file:// and windows drive letters are rejected. The size is checked against max_download_mb (20 MB by default) before the bytes are fetched. This is a read of Telegram but it writes a file, so it sits behind read_only and uses files.write; it does not consume the send-rate budget.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

messageId.description: Id of the message holding the media

path.description: Destination path inside the workspace, for example downloads/photo.jpg

tools.name: mark_read
tools.description: Mark a chat as read for the connected user account, clearing its unread badge. chat must pass allowed_chats. This is a write, so it is blocked when read_only is on, and it counts towards nothing else: no message is sent and the send-rate budget is untouched.

chat.description: @username, t.me/... link or numeric peer id

descriptor.title: Telegram feed post
descriptor.description: Fires when a watched channel or group posts new text that matches the keywords

configFields.label: Channel
configFields.help: Fire only for this channel; empty means every watched channel. You can also type an @username that is not in the list

configFields.label: Keywords
configFields.help: Comma-separated terms; empty matches every post

configFields.label: Exclude words
configFields.help: Comma-separated terms; a post containing any of them is skipped

actions.title: Instance status
actions.description: Filters, per-channel feed watermark and stored post counts, fire counters

actions.title: Reset cursor
actions.description: Drop the channel feed watermark so the next poll treats it as first sight: it baselines silently unless add-on backfill is above zero

peer.description: Configured channel to reset; omit to reset every configured channel
